The Real Cost of Ignoring a Small Leak
ourblog_water_heater_season_is_upon_us.text: id="page" class="container" role="main"> Water heater season is upon us! Oct 1 Written By Bj Zelch As temperatures begin to drop across Utah, your water heater starts working harder to keep up with the demand for hot water. Fall and winter are some of the most common times for homeowners to notice problems with an aging or struggling water heater. From longer recovery times to strange noises, leaks, or running out of hot water altogether, these warning signs shouldn’t be ignored. At Emet Plumbing Heating & Air, we want homeowners to know what to look for before a small water heater issue turns into an unexpected cold shower—or a costly leak. 1. Colder incoming water During fall and winter, the water entering your home is colder. Your water heater has to work harder and longer to bring that water up to your desired temperature. 2. Increased hot water use Colder weather often means longer hot showers, warmer baths, more laundry, holiday guests, and greater overall hot water demand. 3. Older water heaters may start showing their age A water heater that seemed fine during the summer may have trouble keeping up once the workload increases. Older tanks can experience slower recovery times, reduced efficiency, corrosion, or leaks. 4. Sediment buildup can affect performance Minerals and sediment collect at the bottom of traditional tank water heaters over time. A popping or rumbling noise can be a sign of sediment buildup, which may reduce efficiency and make the unit work harder. 5. Small problems can become bigger problems Corrosion, leaking connections, worn components, pressure issues, or a failing tank can become more noticeable when the water heater is operating more frequently. 6. Holiday guests can put your water heater to the test Extra showers, dishes, laundry, and cooking can quickly expose a water heater that is undersized or no longer performing like it should. Don't Wait Until You're Taking a Cold Shower If your water heater has been making strange noises, isn't keeping up with your family's hot water needs, or you're unsure how much life it has left, Emet Plumbing Heating & Air can help. Our experienced technicians can inspect your system, identify potential problems, and help you determine whether maintenance, repair, or replacement makes the most sense for your home. ourblog_the_real_cost_of_ignoring_a_smal.text: id="page" class="container" role="main"> The Real Cost of Ignoring a Small Leak Mar 24 Written By Bj Zelch A small leak might not seem like a big deal. Maybe it’s just a slow drip under the sink or a tiny puddle near your water heater. It’s easy to ignore—until it turns into a much bigger (and more expensive) problem. The truth is, even the smallest plumbing leak can cost you hundreds—or even thousands of dollars over time. Here’s why you should never overlook it: 1. Higher Water Bills A faucet leaking just once per second can waste over 3,000 gallons of water per year. That’s money literally going down the drain. 2. Hidden Structural Damage Leaks can seep into walls, floors, cabinets, and foundations, causing warping, cracking, and costly repairs. 3. Mold and Mildew Growth Mold can begin growing in as little as 24–48 hours, leading to health issues and expensive remediation. Mold and Mildew growth can be found anywhere from your toilet flange, to your tub, shower surroundings, ceilings, sinks and more. 4. Bigger Plumbing Failures Small leaks can signal bigger issues like pipe corrosion or pressure problems, which can lead to major failures. 5. Increased Repair Costs A simple repair can turn into a costly project if ignored. 6. Emergency Situations Leaks can suddenly cause flooding, damaging flooring, furniture, and electrical systems. What You Should Do If you notice dripping sounds, stains, musty smells, or higher water bills—act quickly. Fixing a leak early can save you thousands. Don’t Wait Until It Gets Worse Even a small leak can turn into a major repair overnight. Protect your home and your wallet by taking action now. ourblog_how_to_prepare_your_ac_unit_for_.text: id="page" class="container" role="main"> How to Prepare Your AC Unit for Summer Heat Mar 23 Written By Bj Zelch As temperatures rise, your AC system becomes essential. Preparing early helps avoid breakdowns, reduce energy bills, and keep your home comfortable all summer. 1. Replace or Clean Air Filters Dirty filters restrict airflow, increase energy bills, and reduce indoor air quality. Replace or clean every 1–3 months. 2. Clean Around the Outdoor Unit Remove leaves, dirt, and debris. Keep at least 2–3 feet of clearance and rinse gently with a hose. 3. Inspect Your Thermostat Ensure it's working correctly, replace batteries, and consider upgrading to a smart thermostat. 4. Check Airflow Inside Your Home Make sure vents are open and not blocked. Check for uneven cooling or weak airflow. 5. Test Your AC Early Turn on your system before peak heat. Watch for warm air, strange noises, or unusual smells. 6. Schedule a Professional Tune-Up A technician will inspect components, clean coils, and check refrigerant levels. 7. Seal Air Leaks Seal windows and doors to keep cool air inside and reduce energy costs. Warning Signs Your AC Needs Service: Need Help Getting Your AC Ready? Contact Emet Plumbing Heating & Air today at 801-433-7354 for professional AC maintenance, repairs, and installations. Stay cool and avoid costly breakdowns this summer. ourblog_5_signs_your_water_heater_is_abo.text: id="page" class="container" role="main"> 5 signs your water heater is about to fail Mar 19 Written By Bj Zelch Your water heater is one of the most important (and most overlooked) systems in your home—until it stops working. The last thing any homeowner wants is a cold shower or a flooded utility room. The good news? Your water heater usually gives warning signs before it fails completely. Catching these early can save you from costly damage and unexpected emergencies. Here are five signs your water heater may be on its way out: 1. Inconsistent or No Hot Water If your hot water suddenly runs out faster than usual—or doesn’t get hot at all—it’s a major red flag. 1. A failing heating element 2. Sediment buildup inside the tank 3. A unit nearing the end of its lifespan 2. Strange Noises Coming from the Tank Hearing popping, banging, or rumbling sounds? That’s usually caused by sediment buildup at the bottom of the tank. 1. Reduces efficiency 2. Overheats the tank 3. Leads to cracks or failure 3. Discolored or Rusty Water If your hot water looks brown, rusty, or has a metallic smell, your water heater could be corroding from the inside. 1. The anode rod has worn out 2. The tank is starting to rust 4. Water Leaks Around the Unit Any moisture or pooling water around your water heater is a serious warning sign. 1. Cracks in the tank 2. Loose connections 3. Internal pressure buildup 5.Your Water Heater Is Over 8–12 Years Old Most traditional tank water heaters last about 8 to 12 years. 1. Break down unexpectedly 2. Lose efficiency 3. Require frequent repairs Don’t Wait for a Total Breakdown. A failing water heater rarely fixes itself—and waiting too long can leave you without hot water when you need it most. Need Help with Your Water Heater? At Emet Plumbing Services, we help homeowners quickly diagnose and fix water heater issues before they turn into emergencies. Whether you need a repair or a full replacement, we’ve got you covered. Call Emet Plumbing Services today at 801-433-7354 to schedule an inspection or get a quote. Bonus Tip: Regular maintenance —like flushing your tank once a year—can extend the life of your water heater and help you avoid costly surprises. ourblog_sp5seqfckf120har2h03je3p5uvymx.text: id="page" class="container" role="main"> What to Do If Your Pipe Bursts in Salt Lake City Mar 17 Written By Bj Zelch A burst pipe is one of the most stressful plumbing emergencies a homeowner can face—especially during Salt Lake City’s cold winters. Step 1: Shut Off Your Main Water Supply Immediately. Locate your main shut-off valve and turn it off. Step 2: Drain Remaining Water. Turn on faucets and flush toilets to relieve pressure. Step 3: Turn Off Electricity if water is near outlets or appliances. Step 4: Clean Up Water Quickly using towels, mops, or a wet vacuum. Why Pipes Burst: Freezing temperatures, poor insulation, and old pipes are common causes. When to Call a Plumber: If you see cracks, water pressure drops, or damage spreads. Call Emet Plumbing Services at 801-433-7354 for fast, reliable help in Salt Lake City. Prevention Tips: Insulate pipes, keep heat on, let faucets drip during extreme cold.
